Split the conjunction and use the standard arithmetic-function identities.

- For the first part, view the divisor sum as the Dirichlet convolution \((\mu * \log)(n)\). Möbius inversion applied to
  \[
  \log n=\sum_{d\mid n}\Lambda(d)
  \]
  yields
  \[
  \sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\log d=-\Lambda(n).
  \]
  It remains only to align the integer-to-real cast of `moebius` with the library’s convolution/divisor-sum lemma. The case \(n=0\) should be discharged from the definitions.

- For the second part, invoke the Dirichlet-series representation of `riemannZeta` on the half-plane \(\Re(s)>1\):
  \[
  \zeta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-s}.
  \]
  Rewrite \(n^{-s}\) as \(1/(n^s)\) using complex powers and identify the resulting convergent series with the unconditional `tsum`. The displayed sum ranges over all naturals, but its \(n=0\) term is zero under Mathlib’s conventions for complex powers and division, so it agrees with the positive-integer series. The assumption \(\Re(s)>1\) is essential for absolute summability and for applying the zeta Dirichlet-series theorem.
